question: Why do women have lower PFAS levels than men?
answer: Both bodies took in the same PFAS, and no approved medical treatment removes it. In women, it leaves through menstrual blood, crosses the placenta to the fetus, and flows into breast milk. Men have no such exit, so their levels stay higher until about 50, when menopause usually starts.
move: Periods, birth and breastfeeding let PFAS out of women; men have no exit.
